findings.failure_mode: corrupted path, missing file, or permission error panics the entire task instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>, use .map_err(|e| LoadError::Io(e)) on read_to_string

findings.failure_mode: non-numeric value in field 1 panics the entire task instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: Use .map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid) and return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>

findings.failure_mode: values in range 65536-4294967295 silently truncate to u16 range, corrupting data with no error
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow) to reject out-of-range values

findings.problem: parts[0] - unchecked indexing into split result
findings.failure_mode: empty line or line without comma causes index-out-of-bounds panic
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and pattern-match the Ok( (name, value) ) tuple

findings.problem: parts[1] - unchecked indexing into split result
findings.failure_mode: line with only one field or empty line causes index-out-of-bounds panic
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and pattern-match the Ok((name, value)) tuple

findings.failure_mode: side-channel log leakage in pure logic path; stdout pollution breaks consumer pipelines and adds unbounded I/O to hot path
findings.fix: Remove println entirely. Logging belongs in the shell layer, never in the functional core

findings.problem: load_shards fuses I/O (fs::read_to_string), logging (println), parsing, and domain construction in a single fn
findings.failure_mode: cannot test parsing logic in isolation; I/O side effects contaminate deterministic core; single point of failure across all concerns
findings.fix: Split into: (1) boundary fn load_shards that reads file and calls parse_records, (2) pure fn parse_records(lines: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>

findings.problem: load_shards returns Vec<Record> with no error type; all failures panic
findings.failure_mode: consumer has no way to distinguish IO error from parse error from overflow error; every failure is a task abort
findings.fix: Define enum LoadError { Io(std::io::Error), Invalid, Overflow, TooMany, Allocation } and return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>

findings.problem: No max_items cap, no try_reserve, no iteration limit on lines
findings.failure_mode: unbounded file size causes unbounded Vec allocation and OOM; hostile input triggers resource exhaustion
findings.fix: Accept max_items: usize parameter; call values.try_reserve(max_items).map_err(|_| LoadError::Allocation) after parsing; enforce count <= max_items before push

findings.problem: Record.value is raw u16, not a domain newtype
findings.failure_mode: any u16 value is accepted without domain validation; no enforcement of valid range, units, or semantics
findings.fix: Define struct RecordValue(u16) with a smart constructor that validates domain invariants, store Record { name: RecordName, value: RecordValue }

findings.problem: Record.name is raw String, not a domain newtype
findings.failure_mode: empty strings, whitespace-only names, and non-domain strings are accepted without validation
findings.fix: Define struct RecordName(String) with smart constructor requiring non-empty, trimmed string

findings.problem: split(',').map(…​).collect() into Vec<String> then indexed access
findings.failure_mode: allocates intermediate Vec per line; loses information about how many fields existed (trailing commas produce extra empty strings); indexing is unchecked
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) to get (name, value_str) tuple; parse value_str directly; no intermediate Vec needed

findings.problem: parse::<u32>() then cast to u16 - no checked conversion path
findings.failure_mode: value 70000 parses successfully as u32 then truncates to 44464 as u16, silently producing wrong data
findings.fix: Parse directly as u16 via .parse::<u16>().map_err(...), or use u16::try_from(u32_val).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow)

findings.fix: Add a criterion or custom benchmark measuring parse throughput on representative shard files
